# `silk/yaml/document`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Parse YAML into a compact document, and read values from it.

## When to use
Use [`YamlDocument.parse`](#YamlDocument.impl.parse) to read a configuration file, a lockfile, or any other YAML text whose
shape is not fixed. Read values with [`YamlDocument.field`](#YamlDocument.impl.field), [`YamlDocument.item`](#YamlDocument.impl.item), and the `as...`
functions. Use [`YamlDocument.parseAll`](#YamlDocument.impl.parseAll) for a stream of several documents. Use
`silk.schema.yaml.SchemaYaml` to read YAML straight into a typed value, and `silk.yaml.output` to
write YAML.

## Details
The parser follows YAML 1.2 with the core schema. It reads block mappings and sequences, flow
collections (`[a, b]` and `{a: 1}`), plain, single-quoted, and double-quoted scalars, literal
(`|`) and folded (`>`) block scalars, comments, anchors and aliases, tags, directives, and several
documents in one stream. Mappings keep source order.

A plain scalar is resolved with the core schema: `null`, `~`, and an empty value are null; `true`
and `false` (also capitalized or upper case) are booleans; `12`, `-3`, `0o17`, and `0xff` are
integers; `1.5`, `6e-3`, `.inf`, and `.nan` are floats; everything else is a string. A quoted
scalar is always a string. The tags `!!str`, `!!int`, `!!float`, `!!bool`, `!!null`, and the
non-specific `!` change the resolution. Other tags are accepted and ignored.

An alias is replaced with a copy of the node its anchor names. Merge keys (`<<`) have no special
meaning: `<<` is an ordinary key.

## Errors
- `YamlError` if the text is not valid YAML, repeats a key in one mapping, uses a key that is not
  a scalar, names an alias that is not defined before it, or nests more than `MAX_DEPTH` (128)
  collections. `offset` gives the byte position of the problem.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document.

## Gotchas
A key is always text: the key `1` in `1: one` reads as the string `"1"`, and an empty key as
`""`. A key that is a collection, such as `[a, b]: c` or `? [a, b]`, is refused with
`YamlReason.UnsupportedKey`.

## Examples
### Read fields from a document
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.yaml.document { YamlDocument, YamlError, YamlNode }

effect fn read() -> i32 ! YamlError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let document = run YamlDocument.parse(b"name: Ada\nports:\n  - 80\n  - 443\n")
  let root = YamlDocument.root(&document)
  let name = YamlDocument.field(&document, root, "name") |> YamlDocument.stringAt(&document)
    |> Option<string>.unwrapOr("")
  let port = match YamlDocument.field(&document, root, "ports") {
    Option<YamlNode>.Some { value } => YamlDocument.item(&document, value, 1) |> YamlDocument.i64At(&document)
      |> Option<i64>.unwrapOr(0)
    Option<YamlNode>.None => 0
  }
  if name != "Ada" || port != 443 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! YamlError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run read() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

### Report where a key repeats
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.yaml.document { YamlDocument, YamlError, YamlReason }

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let parsed = run Effect.result(YamlDocument.parse(b"name: Ada\nname: Grace\n")) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return match move parsed {
    Result<YamlDocument, YamlError | OutOfMemoryError>.Success {..} => 1
    Result<YamlDocument, YamlError | OutOfMemoryError>.Failure {error} => match move error {
      // The second `name` starts at byte 10.
      YamlError {reason, offset} => if reason == YamlReason.DuplicateKey && offset == 10 { 0 } else { 2 }
      OutOfMemoryError {} => { fail OutOfMemoryError {} }
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="YamlKind.impl.ofPlain"></a>

### Associated function `ofPlain`

```silk
pub fn ofPlain(text: string) -> YamlKind
```

Returns the kind that the plain (unquoted) scalar `text` resolves to with the YAML 1.2 core
schema.

#### When to use

Check if a string can be written without quotes: if the result is not `YamlKind.String`, a
reader would read the unquoted text as another kind of value.

#### Details

The empty text, `null`, `Null`, `NULL`, and `~` give `YamlKind.Null`. `true` and `false` in
the same three spellings give `YamlKind.Bool`. Decimal, `0o` octal, and `0x` hexadecimal
integers give `YamlKind.Integer`. Decimals with a fraction or an exponent, `.inf`, `-.inf`, and
`.nan` give `YamlKind.Float`. All other text gives `YamlKind.String`. The text is not checked
for characters that a plain scalar cannot hold.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.yaml.document { YamlKind }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  if YamlKind.ofPlain("0x1f") != YamlKind.Integer || YamlKind.ofPlain("yes") != YamlKind.String {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="YamlDocument"></a>

## `YamlDocument`

```silk
pub struct YamlDocument
```

A parsed YAML stream: one or more documents, held as a flat list of values.

### When to use
Use [`YamlDocument.parse`](#YamlDocument.impl.parse) to read one document and [`YamlDocument.parseAll`](#YamlDocument.impl.parseAll) to read a stream of
several. Start reading at [`YamlDocument.root`](#YamlDocument.impl.root), or at [`YamlDocument.documentAt`](#YamlDocument.impl.documentAt) for a stream.

### Details
Strings are decoded when the text is parsed, and numbers are converted. Each value also keeps the
span of its text, which [`YamlDocument.span`](#YamlDocument.impl.span) returns. The document owns all of its text, so it
does not borrow the input.

### Gotchas
A `YamlNode` is only meaningful with the document that returned it.

### Examples
#### Walk the members of a mapping
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.yaml.document { YamlDocument, YamlError, YamlMember }

effect fn total() -> i64 ! YamlError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let document = run YamlDocument.parse(b"a: 1\nb: 2\nc: 3\n")
  let mut members = YamlDocument.members(&document, YamlDocument.root(&document))
  let mut sum: i64 = 0
  while let Option<YamlMember>.Some { value } = members.next(&document) {
    sum = sum + Option<i64>.unwrapOr(YamlDocument.asI64(&document, value.value), 0)
  }
  return sum
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! YamlError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let sum = run total() |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return if sum == 6 { 0 } else { 1 }
}
```

<a id="YamlDocument.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(bytes: &[u8]) -> YamlDocument ! YamlError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `bytes` as one YAML document.

#### Details
The text may start with a `---` marker and end with a `...` marker. Text with no document,
such as an empty file or one with only comments, gives a document whose root is null.

#### Errors
- `YamlError` if `bytes` is not valid YAML, or with `YamlReason.MultipleDocuments` if it holds
  more than one document. `offset` is the byte position of the problem.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document.

<a id="YamlDocument.impl.parseAll"></a>

### Associated function `parseAll`

```silk
pub effect fn parseAll(bytes: &[u8]) -> YamlDocument ! YamlError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Parses `bytes` as a stream of YAML documents, separated by `---` or `...` markers.

#### Details
Read the number of documents with [`YamlDocument.documentCount`](#YamlDocument.impl.documentCount) and each one with
[`YamlDocument.documentAt`](#YamlDocument.impl.documentAt). Text with no document gives a stream with no documents.

#### Errors
- `YamlError` if `bytes` is not valid YAML. `offset` is the byte position of the problem.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the document.

<a id="YamlDocument.impl.scalarText"></a>

### Method `scalarText`

```silk
pub fn scalarText<'a>(self: &'a Self, node: YamlNode) -> Option<string<'a>>
```

Returns the text of a scalar: the decoded text of a string, or the source spelling of a null,
a boolean, or a number, such as `0x1F` or `~`. Returns `None` for a sequence or a mapping. The
text borrows the document.

#### When to use
Use it to read a value as text whatever it resolved to, such as a version `1.10` that the core
schema reads as a float.
